core_obligations: Set b' = b o g and denote by g_infinity : W'_infinity -> W_infinity the restriction of g, and by i'_infinity the inclusion of W'_infinity (proof lines 10117-10119).

For alpha in CH_k(X) choose beta' in CH_{k+1}(W') restricting to the flat pullback of alpha on (b')^{-1}A^1_X, and verify that beta = g_*beta' restricts to the flat pullback of alpha on b^{-1}A^1_X, so that beta may be used in the definition of C (proof lines 10120-10123).

Conclude i_infinity^* beta = g_{infinity,*}(i'_infinity)^* beta' by the compatibility of the Gysin map with proper pushforward, and deduce the identity of bivariant classes, the same holding after any base change by X' -> X locally of finite type (proof lines 10124-10128).
proof_roadmap: Set up the comparison of the two models and their infinity loci (proof lines 10117-10119).
Produce compatible cycle representatives beta' and beta = g_*beta' (proof lines 10120-10123).
Apply the Gysin-pushforward compatibility and conclude (proof lines 10124-10128).
difficulty_reason: Extending the Gysin-at-infinity lemma, the statement says that for a proper morphism g : W' -> W which is an isomorphism over A^1_X, the classes C' in A^0(W'_infinity -> X) and C in A^0(W_infinity -> X) constructed there satisfy g_{infinity,*} o C' = C (statement lines 10107-10114). The proof sets b' = b o g, writes i'_infinity for the inclusion of W'_infinity, and compares the two constructions on a single cycle class: for alpha in CH_k(X) one chooses beta' in CH_{k+1}(W') restricting to the flat pullback of alpha on (b')^{-1}A^1_X, observes that its pushforward beta = g_*beta' restricts to the flat pullback of alpha on b^{-1}A^1_X, so beta is an admissible choice in the definition of C, and then invokes the compatibility of the Gysin map with the proper pushforward to get i_infinity^* beta = g_{infinity,*}(i'_infinity)^* beta' (proof lines 10116-10125). Since this holds after any base change by X' -> X locally of finite type, the two classes agree (proof lines 10126-10128). Choosing beta as a pushforward so that both constructions compute the same value is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
